post.summary: Record a relationship between two residents
post.description: Needs family.manage. Resident to resident, so it survives either person moving; stored in one canonical direction (see RelationshipKind). Both people must be on file and in the writer's scope: the resident in the path answers 404 when not, the other person 409 resident-not-found. An own-barangay account works in its barangay; an assigned-cases account is 403, as on the resident registry. The same link already standing (either way round for spouse-of and sibling-of) answers 200 with the standing relationship and records nothing, so a retried request never records a second marriage. Otherwise 201: relationship-recorded is appended to office_family_events with the reason, and audit office_relationship.recorded. A parent-of that reverses a parent link already on file is 409 contradicts-existing.

get.description: Needs household.view. An address and who lives there, recorded by staff — not the residents' app households (/api/v1/households); nothing is shared between the two. By reference number. An own-barangay account sees only its barangay; an assigned-cases account is 403, as on the resident registry. q matches every word (up to five) against the reference number, the head's surname and the street address, but not the street address of a protected household for a reader without request.view-sensitive. resident_id answers which household a person is in. minimum_band filters on the advisory band; to fill such a page up to 500 rows are read per request, so a short page can still say has_more. head is the resident registry's redacted record. band is the same for every role, computed from the unredacted records; present_factor_count counts the factors present as this reader is shown them. Nothing here decides eligibility. Every member of a household with a protected member, or of a family with one or living in a household that has one, also has street_address and purok_or_sitio withheld from that reader (withheld names exact_address): people who share a record usually share a roof, and a member's address listed beside the masked one would say where the protected person lives.

get.description: Needs household.view. The household, its current members (head first, then in the order they joined) as the resident registry's redacted records, its vulnerability snapshot, and its events newest first. Out of scope answers 404, exactly as one that does not exist. A household with a member under vawc-survivor or cicl (is_protected) withholds street_address and purok_or_sitio from a reader without request.view-sensitive (withheld: ["exact_address"]), because that address is where the protected person lives. For that reader the protected-member factor reads withheld, with an empty basis, origin computed and no correction, and its correction events are left out; likewise the two income factors for a reader without resident.view-sensitive; the band is not recomputed, so every role reads the same band. Every member of a household with a protected member, or of a family with one or living in a household that has one, also has street_address and purok_or_sitio withheld from that reader (withheld names exact_address): people who share a record usually share a roof, and a member's address listed beside the masked one would say where the protected person lives.

post.summary: Change who lives in a household
post.description: Needs household.manage. Intents, not a replacement list: add-member, remove-member, change-role, set-head, applied in order, all or none, against the locked household and every person named — so a change from a stale screen is refused rather than discarding a member somebody else added. set-head makes the outgoing head a relative, which a person can correct. The head is removed only when the same change names another. A person joins only if on file, in the writer's scope (otherwise member-not-found) and in no other household. One reason for the whole change; one event per intent in office_household_events, each with that reason; audit office_household.membership_changed.

By reference number; dissolved families only with include_dissolved=true. An own-barangay account sees a family whose household is in its barangay, or — with no household — one whose every current member is recorded as living there; an assigned-cases account is 403. q matches every word (up to five) against the reference number, the family's name and the current head's surname. barangay_id is the household's barangay, so it leaves out families with no household. Every member of a household with a protected member, or of a family with one or living in a household that has one, also has street_address and purok_or_sitio withheld from that reader (withheld names exact_address): people who share a record usually share a roof, and a member's address listed beside the masked one would say where the protected person lives.

post.description: Needs family.manage. Out of one family and into another as one act, so nobody is dropped from every family on file halfway. from_family_id null joins a family; to_family_id null leaves one; never both. The person and each family named must be on file and in the writer's scope (otherwise resident-not-found or family-not-found). Leaving closes the person's membership period (left_on); joining opens a new one with role. With move_household and a destination family that has a household, the person also moves out of their current household and into that one as a relative, recorded there as member-removed and member-added with the same reason. The reason is at least 8 characters. A transfer that has already landed answers 200 and records nothing. Appends resident-transferred to office_family_events; audit office_family.transferred, against the resident. Answers the destination family, or the family left when there is none.

get.description: A name over a list's query parameters. Reading the views of a list needs the key that opens it: residents resident.view, beneficiaries beneficiary.view, assistance-requests request.view, releases release.view, cases case.view, households household.view; an account with none of them is 403 before the query is read. The office's shared views first, then the reader's own, each by name; somebody else's personal view is never listed. A view whose sector parameter is vawc-survivor or cicl is left out for a reader without request.view-sensitive, because its name can describe that population. Whole, never paged: the caps bound it. Not scoped by barangay: a view holds no records, and the list it opens applies the reader's scope.

remarks.description: Required for waived, rejected and needs-replacement.

OfficeDocumentUpload.description: multipart/form-data. A form cannot say null: a field left out is null.

file.description: Required for uploaded and scanned; refused for encoded and external-verification. A PDF, JPEG or PNG by its bytes, 10 MB at most.

replaces_because.description: Required when a version is already in force; ignored on the first.

handle.description: Opaque, single-use, five minutes; exchanged for the bytes by the same account at POST /api/v1/office/document-files. Kept here only as its hash.

redacted_for_sharing.description: This server keeps the copy the office received and makes no other.

warning.description: Composed here, to show before the file opens: what it is, how to handle it (protected sector or RA 10173), that opening it is recorded, and that nothing was redacted.

OfficeDocumentRequestChannel.description: No email: the LGU supplied no relay.

state.description: answered when a version is recorded for the document; withdrawn with a reason. Closed once, never removed.

message.description: What the applicant was told. Null when withheld.

withdrawn_reason.description: Null when answered, open, or withheld.

is_withheld.description: A protected request read without request.view-sensitive: the words are withheld, the entry is listed.

data.description: Whole: open first, then the most recently asked.

OfficeCaseStatus.description: The console’s CaseStatus. closed is terminal: there is no reopening, and a recurrence is a new case naming the old one.

OfficeCaseCategory.description: How a supervisor finds a file. Drives nothing.

OfficeCaseQueue.description: The console’s queues, counted on the municipality’s calendar. Closed cases fall out of every queue but all. due-soon is within 7 days; stalled is 30 days or more since anything was recorded.

OfficeCaseWithheld.description: summary, reasons, task_words and notes: the case is about a person under vawc-survivor or cicl today and the reader lacks request.view-sensitive. household_context: the reader’s scope is a caseload, which a case does not widen to the registry — household_id is null and the household is not named.

OfficeCaseTask.description: What the office undertook to do, by when, and who owes it. The next action is the open task due soonest — never derived from the status.

outcome.description: What happened, in the words of whoever completed it. Null while open, or when withheld.

OfficeCaseNote.description: Listed for every reader of the case. The body is null, and is_withheld true, for a protected note read without case-note.view-protected, or any note on a protected person’s case read without request.view-sensitive.

OfficeCaseEvent.description: One immutable line of the case’s history: identifiers and enum values, and the reason. Never edited or deleted.

reason.description: Null when withheld: see withheld.reasons. For task-completed it is the outcome.

staff_user_id.description: Who was given the case or the task; null for unassigned and for a task returned to nobody.

due_on.description: The new date of a rescheduled task.

OfficeCase.description: A case as a list or a queue shows it, already redacted for the reader.

reference_number.description: CASE-YYYY-NNNNNN, issued when the case is opened.

subject.description: The person the case is about, as the resident registry discloses them to this reader.

household_id.description: The subject’s household today; null when they have none, or when withheld (household_context).

barangay_id.description: The subject’s barangay when the case was opened, kept.

summary.description: The presenting problem. Null when withheld (summary).

linked_request_ids.description: Every request the case names, in the order linked — including any this reader may not read.

continues_case_id.description: The closed case this one continues. Never a reopening.

open_request_count.description: Linked requests not over, among those this reader may read.

last_activity_at.description: The latest of the case’s events and the moves of the requests it names.

OfficeCaseWorkspace.description: Everything a caseworker needs to act, in one read. Every mutation answers with this, read after the change.

requests.description: The linked requests this reader may read under the request’s own scope and key (request.view), newest filed first, each disclosed as GET /office/assistance-requests/{id} discloses it. A case is never a way round a request’s scope.

data.description: Every queue, in the console’s order.
